name: MonarchAiOnboardingTour
title: AiOnboardingTour
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager of steps with MonarchStepper and MonarchButton, presented by the app in MonarchBottomSheet or inline
summary: A short, step-by-step introduction to AI in a product (what it can see, what it can do, how to turn it off) with Back, Next and Turn off AI on every step.
whenToUse: The first time someone meets an AI feature, to explain in a few steps what it sees, what it does and how to turn it off, before they rely on it.
whenNotToUse: For a one-line note about AI use MonarchAiDisclaimer. For a general product walkthrough that is not about AI use a pager of your own or MonarchStepper. To point at one control, use a Material 3 tooltip.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiOnboardingTour(steps: List<MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep>, step: Int, onStepChange: (Int) -> Unit, onDisable: () -> Unit, onFinish: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, skipIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels = MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(), onSkip: (() -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchAiOnboardingTour(steps: List<MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep>, onDisable: () -> Unit, onFinish: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, skipIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels = MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(), onSkip: (() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep(title: String, body: String, id: String? = null)

class MonarchAiOnboardingTourLabels(eyebrow: String? = null, stepOf: ((step: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, back: String? = null, next: String? = null, finish: String? = null, skip: String? = null, disable: String? = null)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, each with a title and a body.

options.name: step
options.description: The position of the current step, from 0, when the app keeps it. Kept inside the steps. The other overload keeps it itself.

options.name: onStepChange
options.description: Called with the new position by Back, Next and a swipe.

options.name: onDisable
options.description: Called by Turn off AI, which is on every step.

options.name: onFinish
options.description: Called by the last step's Got it button.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph beside the eyebrow, in the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: skipIcon
options.description: The icon of the skip button; without it the button shows the words Skip introduction.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces "AI", "Step … of …", Back, Next, Got it, Skip introduction and Turn off AI.

options.name: onSkip
options.description: Adds a button that skips the tour.

states.name: first step
states.description: Next and Turn off AI; no Back.

states.name: middle step
states.description: Back, Next and Turn off AI.

states.name: last step
states.description: Back, Got it and Turn off AI.

states.name: one step
states.description: Got it and Turn off AI, without the stepper.

states.name: no steps
states.description: The eyebrow and the buttons only.

appearance: The eyebrow in caption type and the AI strong color, then MonarchStepper (compact when the names do not fit), the step title in the heading style and default text, the body in muted text. Next and Got it are primary buttons, Back secondary and Turn off AI ghost; the skip button is ghost or an icon button in the muted text color.
platformNotes: The web's target option, which outlines an element on the page, has no equivalent: point at a control with a Material 3 tooltip. The web's floating placement becomes a sheet the app presents (MonarchBottomSheet), as on iOS. Steps can be swiped as well as moved with Back and Next. iOS has an internal-state and a Binding initialiser; Android has an uncontrolled overload and a controlled one with step and onStepChange. iOS steps take an SF Symbol; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so there is one icon slot for the tour and none per step. The close button is a skip button whose icon is a slot; without an icon it shows its words. The web's controlled defaultStep is the uncontrolled overload, which starts at the first step. TalkBack focus is not moved when the step changes (Compose has no API to move accessibility focus); the step and its title are announced through a polite live region instead. Pages are composed ahead so the pager measures every step, but its height follows the page in view and may change between steps of different lengths.
accessibility: Each step's title is a heading.
When the step changes, "Step 2 of 4" and the step's title are announced through a polite live region; nothing is announced when the tour appears.
MonarchStepper reads the position and the name of the step.
Turn off AI is on every step, so the opt-out is always reachable.
Every button has a 48dp touch target; the buttons wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.
The skip icon button is named "Skip introduction".
edgeCases: A step outside the range is clamped to the first or the last step.
Step ids default to the position; the stepper always gets unique ids even when titles repeat.
With one step there is no stepper; with no steps only the eyebrow and buttons show, and the primary button is Got it.
Long titles and bodies wrap at large text sizes.

examples.title: Inline, pointing at a button
The step kept by the app
examples.setup:
var step by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
var aiOn by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
examples.code:
MonarchAiOnboardingTour(
    steps = listOf(
        MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep("What it can do", "Draft replies. You review before anything is sent."),
        MonarchAiOnboardingTourStep("How to turn it off", "Settings, then AI."),
    ),
    step = step,
    onStepChange = { step = it },
    onDisable = { aiOn = false },
    onFinish = { step = 0 },
)
